title: Concerning Those Who Have Obtained a Principality by Wickedness
coreMove: Separate seizure by wickedness from glory, then judge whether injury is concentrated for security or multiplied from insecurity.
sourcePressure: The source uses Agathocles and Oliverotto to show that wicked seizure can gain and hold power without deserving glory. Its operational distinction is between severities used at one stroke for security and repeated cruelties that keep subjects unsettled, unattached, and unable to trust the ruler.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong version says cruelty works or that the ends justify the means. The writer must hold both points at once: wickedness may gain empire but not glory, and repeated injuries reveal a ruler who is still unsafe.

counterintuition: most people assume cruelty is bad, but actually it can work
violence is sometimes necessary, full stop
tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds and list hard choices
think of where you need to be ruthless
write a plan to cut enemies out of your life

exampleSpecs.domain: a palace guard captain seizing a citadel after inviting senior officers to a dawn oath ceremony
exampleSpecs.audience: a historian explaining why the coup held but never became honorable rule
exampleSpecs.stakes: the captain removes rivals in one morning, but every later arrest either settles the new order or proves he must keep the blade visible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The historian places the single dawn casualty list beside a later stack of weekly arrest orders and draws the line where seizure ends and repeated insecurity begins.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A dawn casualty list lies beside a stack of weekly arrest orders.

exampleSpecs.domain: a mining concession boss taking over a remote camp through forged safety charges against rival foremen
exampleSpecs.audience: a magistrate deciding whether the camp is stable or merely silenced
exampleSpecs.stakes: miners may accept one purge if tunnels reopen, but monthly fabricated charges keep every crew waiting for the next injury
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The magistrate compares the first sealed dismissal packet with the new row of false safety tags hanging on foremen's bunks, showing injuries multiplying instead of decreasing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: False safety tags hang from six empty foremen's bunks.

exampleSpecs.domain: a frontier fortress quartermaster who poisons the old command council and then ration-books the garrison
exampleSpecs.audience: a military judge reviewing why soldiers obeyed during siege but refused to praise him afterward
exampleSpecs.stakes: the fortress survived external attack, but survival cannot convert treachery against friends into glory
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The judge taps the ration book that saved the siege, then points to the stained council cups and says one explains holding power while the other bars honor.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Stained council cups sit beside a fortress ration book.

exampleSpecs.domain: a city tax farmer using one mass confiscation to break armed smuggling families, then choosing whether to keep raiding shops
exampleSpecs.audience: an adviser warning that repeated small seizures create more hatred than the first blow settled
exampleSpecs.stakes: security may require disarming smuggling houses, but daily raids teach ordinary shopkeepers that no property is safe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The adviser takes the confiscation ledger off the raid cart and closes it before the captain can add ordinary shop stalls to the second-day list.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A confiscation ledger slides across the rail of a raid cart.

exampleSpecs.domain: a rebel radio commander seizing a capital broadcaster through betrayal of allied announcers
exampleSpecs.audience: listeners trying to read whether the new voice has secured the station or still fears it
exampleSpecs.stakes: one seizure can control the signal, but nightly denunciations show the commander cannot let people settle into obedience
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The first broadcast ends with a promised amnesty list, but the next three nights the commander scratches more names into the black transmission log while the studio clock blinks past midnight.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A black transmission log lies open below a blinking studio clock.

exampleSpecs.domain: a port guildmaster winning leadership by trapping rivals in a rigged audit and then distributing dock repairs
exampleSpecs.audience: a guild apprentice learning why benefits must follow if the first injury is not to become daily fear
exampleSpecs.stakes: dockworkers might accept the destroyed rival houses if the port becomes safer, but no attachment forms while surprise audits continue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The guildmaster sets down the rigged audit stamp, unlocks the repair chest, and the apprentice notices whether the stamp stays on the desk or goes back into his sleeve.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A rigged audit stamp sits beside an unlocked dock repair chest.

skillTargets: distinguish gaining power by wickedness from gaining glory or legitimate excellence
identify whether severities are concentrated in one security act or multiplied over time
analyze how repeated injuries prevent subjects from attaching themselves to the ruler
evaluate whether later benefits are credible or dismissed as forced because harsh measures came too late

tryThisNowSpec: Take one harsh consolidation in history. Make two columns: injuries done once to secure the new order, and injuries repeated afterward because the ruler still did not feel safe.
